question: Two compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**structural isomers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Structural isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different structural formulas.
 
• These isomers differ in the connectivity of their atoms and the sequence in which the atoms are bonded.
 
• Structural isomerism is also known as constitutional isomerism.
 
• This type of isomerism includes chain isomerism, position isomerism, and functional group isomerism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes**: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• **Valency**: The combining capacity of an element, often determined by the number of electrons in the outer shell.
 
• **Allotropes**: Different structural forms of the same element in the same physical state, like graphite and diamond for carbon.
 
• **Stereoisomers**: Isomers that have the same molecular formula and connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms.
